name: Imst
kurzbeschreibung: The carnival capital of Tirol, famous for its time-honored Schellerlaufen in the Gurgltal valley.
beschreibung:
Overview

Imst is located at an altitude of 827 metres in the Tyrolean Upper Inn Valley and serves as the bustling administrative capital of the Imst district. Strategically situated at the mouth of the Gurgl Valley where it meets the Inn, beneath the dramatic Muttekopf massif, the town spans 113 square kilometres and is home to around 11,000 residents. Divided into historic Upper and Lower Town quarters, Imst is celebrated as the Town of Fountains, boasting over 40 fresh spring-water fountains. Simultaneously, it stands as an international hub for mountaineers and rock climbers. The municipality blends charming alpine urbanity with dramatic limestone peaks, rich craft heritage, and deeply rooted living folklore.

History

The origins of Imst stretch back to antiquity, with its first recorded mention appearing in AD 763 as oppidum humiste. During the 15th and 16th centuries, the town flourished through silver and lead mining, which gave rise to the prestigious Imst Masons' Guild. Global fame arrived in the 18th and 19th centuries courtesy of the intrepid Imst bird sellers, who bred song canaries and traded them across Europe. The late-Gothic Parish Church of the Assumption features an 84.5-metre spire, the tallest church tower in Tyrol. The crowning cultural treasure is the Imst Schemenlaufen carnival: Featuring the iconic masked figures Roller and Scheller, this centuries-old ritual was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2012.

Getting There

Imst is a pivotal transport crossroads in Western Austria. By automobile, the town is accessed via the Inntal Motorway A12 using the Imst-Au and Imst-Pitzenhöfe exits, or toll-free from Bavaria across the scenic Fern Pass highway B179. Train passengers arrive at Imst-Pitztal railway station, an essential stop on the transalpine Arlberg Railway serviced by ÖBB Railjet expresses and Tyrol S-Bahn lines S4 and S5. A comprehensive network of municipal city buses and VVT regional lines provides seamless transit connecting the station, town centre, Hoch-Imst resort, and neighbouring valleys.

Tips

A signature natural wonder is hiking through the wild Rosengarten Gorge (Rosengartenschlucht), starting right in the town centre and ascending via wooden catwalks and carved rock tunnels along the Schinderbach stream to the mystical Blue Grotto cave in Hoch-Imst. There, adrenaline seekers will love the Alpine Coaster Imst—with a track length of 3,525 metres, it is the longest alpine roller coaster in the world. Sport climbing enthusiasts flock to the Imst Climbing Centre and demanding via ferratas on Mount Muttekopf. Heritage lovers should tour the House of Fasnacht museum to marvel at the hand-carved masks of the Schemenlaufen tradition.
